Next you'll probably want to start reading business publications to get a feel for the "market" (i.e. Europe is imploding right now starting with Greece, then moving to Ireland, Portugal, and Spain). This way you'll know which investments you think is a good idea and which are more risky.

ELI5 how a silencer on a handgun or rifle works (like in the movies).

The silencer basically allows the gases to escape slower, cools the hot gas, and disperses the gas over an increased area than just at the tip of the barrel. The gas takes more time to leave the silencer, which creates a reduction of sound.

Edit: also because the gas is cooled and dispersed, the typical 'flash' of a gunshot is pretty much eliminated in most cases.

Technically it's called a "suppressor", and I'll start off by saying that suppressors in movies and games giving that nice little muffled "pew!" sound is bullshit. In reality it's more of a sharp crack.

Glock 17: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nBofwiYwGho
AR15: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NM8xvE5B4yk

In reality it would sound even louder than in the videos, since the camera's auto-volume is ducking the volume when he fires to prevent the sound from clipping.

The inside of a suppressor has a bunch of air pockets and baffles for the sound waves and expanding gasses to get lost in

http://i.imgur.com/u9kpEov.jpg http://i.imgur.com/VISHdPh.jpg

The ammunition needed for a suppressor to work properly has to be "subsonic" ammo, meaning it isn't as powerful/fast and never breaks the sound barrier, which would create a sonic crack. Since subsonic ammunition travels at a slower speed, range and power are reduced, and you have to lead moving targets more and compensate more for bullet drop at range.

Fantastic explanation, /u/JohnnyPemberton, but I'd like to add my ten cents.

The inside of a suppressor has a bunch of air pockets and baffles for the sound waves and expanding gasses to get lost in

Guns work by using expanding gasses to push the bullet out of the barrel. Once the gasses get the bullet out, they keep expanding out of the barrel until the air pressure is the same inside the barrel as outside it. All those expanding gasses come out of the barrel really fast, similarly to the way pressurised (and therefore expanding when you let them out) gasses come out of a balloon fairly quickly when it pops. Think of a suppressor as a way to let the air out of the "balloon" more slowly so you can get the air out (make the air pressure the same inside the balloon as outside it) without making as much noise.

Technically it's called a "suppressor"

However, a lot of legislation (including the US NFA) does still refer to them as "silencers," in part because the first one commercially marketed was branded the "Maxim Silencer."

A lot of the core functionality of Java will remain the same between the versions. There are some new niceties in Java 8 like a Date Time library that doesn't suck and Lambda Expressions and of corse security updates.

The differences between Java 7 and Java 8 are extremely significant, and I recommend reading through a book that explicitly covers Java 8 once you've mastered Java through version 7. But that being said, you can definitely learn the overwhelming lion's share of Java via any book through version 7. Java 8 introduces a new paradigm of development, and it takes a while to wrap your head around it if you've never been exposed to it. Java 8 adds on to Java 7 - everything you acquire through Java 7 will be relevant to Java 8. A book that has really helped me out for Java 8 is Java 8 In Action
